newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech fears FCC policies are outdated.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech fears FCC policies are outdated.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said it is concerned the U.S. Federal Communications Commission has adopted outdated policies in its overhaul of the nation's telephone charges announced Wednesday.

"As an industry, we cannot hope to arrive any time soon in the sort of competitive communications market envisioned by policy makers, and that customers now expect, if the FCC has its eyes focused on the rear view mirror of the past," Gary Lytle, Ameritech's vice president, federal relations, said in a statement.

On Wednesday regulators adopted new rules stemming from last year's Telecommunications Act. As a result of the rules, the FCC predicts phone costs to residential and business phone customers will decline by $25 billion over the next five years.

Ameritech said the overhaul includes regulations similar to rate of return rules which were abandoned over the last few years in all five of the Baby Bell's Midwest regional states. The company said the policy, which is an increased productivity factor, is retroactive to July 1996.

"We'll reserve detailed comment until we've examined the order point by point. However, based on what we know, we are concerned that the FCC, in its haste to issue a timely order, injected relics of the past," Lytle said.
